question: How do I access the current page's frontmatter and site metadata at runtime?
expected_answer: Use the `useData()` composable from `vitepress`. It returns reactive refs including `site`, `theme`, `page`, `frontmatter`, `params`, `lang`, `dir`, `localeIndex`, and `title`.

question: How do I get the current route inside a custom theme component?
expected_answer: Import `useRoute` from `vitepress`. It returns a reactive route object with `path`, `data`, and `component` for the current page.

question: How do I navigate programmatically from one page to another?
expected_answer: Use `useRouter()` from `vitepress` and call `router.go(path)`. The router also exposes `onBeforeRouteChange` and `onAfterRouteChange` hooks for navigation lifecycle.

question: How do I prefix an asset URL with the configured base path?
expected_answer: Wrap the path with `withBase()` from `vitepress`, e.g. `withBase('/icon.png')`. This is needed when the site is deployed under a non-root base.

question: How do I render content that should only run in the browser?
expected_answer: Wrap the content in the built-in `<ClientOnly>` component. Anything inside it is rendered only on the client, skipping SSR.

question: How do I load data from local files at build time and use it in pages?
expected_answer: Create a `*.data.ts` file that exports `default defineLoader({ ... })` or use `createContentLoader('glob', options)` to scan a glob of markdown files. Import the default export from any page or component to access the data.

question: What is the configuration entry point and how do I get type hints?
expected_answer: Place `.vitepress/config.ts` in your project and wrap the export with `defineConfig()` from `vitepress`. Use `defineConfigWithTheme<ThemeConfig>()` when you have a custom theme config type.

question: How do I deploy a VitePress site under a sub-path like `/docs/`?
expected_answer: Set `base: '/docs/'` in `.vitepress/config.ts`. All asset URLs and internal links will be rewritten to include the base. Use `withBase()` for runtime-resolved asset paths.

question: How do I remove the .html extension from generated URLs?
expected_answer: Set `cleanUrls: true` in `.vitepress/config.ts`. The build will produce directory-style URLs (e.g. `/guide/`) that work on hosts that handle `index.html` resolution.

question: How do I rewrite source paths to different output URLs?
expected_answer: Use the `rewrites` option in site config: `rewrites: { 'packages/:pkg/:slug.md': ':pkg/:slug.md' }`. Each rule maps a source path pattern to the desired output URL pattern.

question: How do I configure the sidebar with multi-section grouping?
expected_answer: In `themeConfig.sidebar`, pass a record keyed by URL prefix where each value is an array of groups: `{ '/guide/': [{ text: 'Intro', items: [{ text: 'Hello', link: '/guide/hello' }] }] }`. Items can have `collapsed: false` to start expanded.

question: How do I add a top navigation menu with dropdowns?
expected_answer: Set `themeConfig.nav` to an array of `NavItem`s. Each item is either `{ text, link }` or `{ text, items: [...] }` for a dropdown. Use `activeMatch` to control which path triggers the active style.

question: How do I enable Algolia DocSearch?
expected_answer: Set `themeConfig.search.provider = 'algolia'` and pass `themeConfig.search.options = { appId, apiKey, indexName }`. Alternatively, use `provider: 'local'` for built-in client-side search.

question: How do I enable local search instead of Algolia?
expected_answer: Set `themeConfig.search = { provider: 'local' }`. This builds a small client-side search index at build time and avoids any external service.

question: How do I configure the homepage hero and features?
expected_answer: Set `layout: home` in the index page's frontmatter, then add `hero: { name, text, tagline, actions }` and `features: [{ title, details }]`. The default theme renders the home layout from these fields.

question: How do I render a team members page?
expected_answer: Use the `<VPTeamMembers>` component (size `medium` or `small`) and pass an array of members `{ avatar, name, title, links }`. For richer layouts, wrap with `<VPTeamPage>`, `<VPTeamPageTitle>`, and `<VPTeamPageSection>`.

question: How do I add custom <head> tags like favicons and Google Fonts?
expected_answer: Use the `head` array in site config. Each entry is `[tag, attrs, innerContent?]`, e.g. `['link', { rel: 'icon', href: '/favicon.ico' }]`. Use `transformHead(context)` for per-page head injection.

question: How do I run code at the end of the build?
expected_answer: Define `buildEnd(siteConfig)` in your site config. It receives the resolved site config and runs after the static build completes, e.g. for sitemap generation or post-processing.

question: How do I generate a sitemap.xml?
expected_answer: Set `sitemap: { hostname: 'https://example.com' }` in site config. VitePress writes `sitemap.xml` to the output directory at the end of the build.

question: How do I extend the default theme with custom components?
expected_answer: Create `.vitepress/theme/index.ts` that exports `{ extends: DefaultTheme, Layout, enhanceApp({ app, router, siteData }) }`. Register custom components via `app.component(name, comp)` inside `enhanceApp`.

question: How do I write a fully custom theme?
expected_answer: Create `.vitepress/theme/index.ts` exporting `{ Layout, enhanceApp? }` where `Layout` is a Vue component. Use `<Content />` to render the current page's markdown. Register globals through `enhanceApp`.

question: How do I render the current page's content inside a custom layout?
expected_answer: Use the `<Content />` component from the runtime. It renders the current page's markdown inside whatever layout you provide.

question: How do I customize syntax highlighting?
expected_answer: Configure `markdown.theme` (a Shiki theme name or `{ light, dark }` pair) and `markdown.lineNumbers` in site config. Pass `markdown.config(md)` to register additional markdown-it plugins.

question: How do I show line numbers in code blocks globally?
expected_answer: Set `markdown: { lineNumbers: true }` in site config. Per-block override with `:line-numbers` after the language tag in the fence.

question: How do I configure dark mode behavior?
expected_answer: Set `themeConfig.appearance` to `true` (default with toggle), `false` (force light), `'force-dark'`, or `'force-auto'`. The default theme reads system preference on first visit.

question: How do I show a Last Updated timestamp on pages?
expected_answer: Set `lastUpdated: true` at the site config level (uses git mtime), then enable display via `themeConfig.lastUpdated = { text: 'Updated', formatOptions: { ... } }`.

question: How do I add an Edit on GitHub link to each page?
expected_answer: Set `themeConfig.editLink = { pattern: 'https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/edit/main/docs/:path', text: 'Edit this page' }`. The `:path` token is replaced per page.

question: How do I configure social links in the navigation?
expected_answer: Set `themeConfig.socialLinks` to an array of `{ icon, link }` items. Built-in icons include 'github', 'twitter', 'discord', 'mastodon', 'youtube', or pass `{ svg: '<svg ...>' }` for a custom icon.

question: How do I configure the right-side outline (table of contents)?
expected_answer: Set `themeConfig.outline = { level, label }` (e.g. `level: [2, 3]`) or `outline: 'deep'` for h2-h6. Disable per page with frontmatter `outline: false`.

question: How do I show or hide the right-side aside?
expected_answer: Use frontmatter `aside: false` to hide it on a page, or set `themeConfig.aside = false` globally. Set `aside: 'left'` to move it to the left.

question: How do I set up i18n with multiple locales?
expected_answer: Use the `locales` site config to declare each locale's `label`, `lang`, `link`, and `themeConfig`. Place locale content under matching subdirectories (e.g. `en/`, `zh/`). VitePress generates a language switcher in the nav.

question: How do I use a Vue component inside a markdown file?
expected_answer: Either register the component globally via `enhanceApp` and use it directly, or import it inline using a `<script setup>` block at the top of the markdown file. Markdown content renders alongside Vue components.

question: How do I import images and assets from markdown?
expected_answer: Reference public assets with absolute paths (`/icon.png` resolves against `public/`). Reference imported assets via standard markdown image syntax — Vite hashes the URL at build time. Use `withBase()` for runtime-resolved paths.

question: How do I run VitePress in development and build for production?
expected_answer: Use the `vitepress dev [root]` command for the dev server with HMR, `vitepress build [root]` to produce the static output, and `vitepress preview [root]` to serve the build locally.

question: How do I scaffold a new VitePress site?
expected_answer: Run `npx vitepress init` and follow the interactive prompts. It writes `.vitepress/config.ts`, an `index.md`, theme defaults, and adds the relevant scripts to `package.json`.

question: How do I deploy a VitePress site to GitHub Pages?
expected_answer: Set `base: '/<repo>/'` in site config, build with `vitepress build docs`, then publish the `docs/.vitepress/dist` directory via a GitHub Actions workflow that runs `actions/deploy-pages@v4`.

question: How do I migrate from VuePress to VitePress?
expected_answer: Move docs into the new structure (`.vitepress/config.ts`), rewrite plugin-style Vue config into `enhanceApp`, replace `<router-link>` with internal markdown links, and migrate theme components to the new theme API. The migration guide lists removed and renamed config keys.

question: How do I add custom routes that aren't backed by a markdown file?
expected_answer: Use a `paths()` dynamic route (`[param].md`) to generate pages at build time, or inject runtime routes via `router.go` with `app.runtime` configuration. Dynamic routes export `paths()` returning route param objects.

question: How do I render the same content in multi-page (MPA) mode?
expected_answer: Set `mpa: true` in site config (experimental). VitePress emits one HTML per page without a client-side router, useful for content-heavy sites where SPA navigation isn't needed.

question: What SSR-safe patterns must I follow in custom components?
expected_answer: Avoid accessing `window`, `document`, or `localStorage` outside `onMounted` or a `<ClientOnly>` boundary. Use `import.meta.env.SSR` to gate server-only code. Lazy-import browser-only deps via dynamic `import()` inside `onMounted`.

question: How do I ignore broken links during build?
expected_answer: Set `ignoreDeadLinks: true` in site config, or pass an array of regex patterns/strings to ignore selectively. Use `'localhostLinks'` to ignore only localhost references.

question: How do I change the source directory and output directory?
expected_answer: Set `srcDir` (default: project root) and `outDir` (default: `<root>/.vitepress/dist`) in site config. Use `srcExclude` (an array of micromatch patterns) to skip files inside `srcDir`.

question: How do I access frontmatter values inside a markdown file template expression?
expected_answer: Use the `$frontmatter` template global (e.g. `{{ $frontmatter.title }}`). For dynamic routes, `$params` exposes the matched route params object.

question: How do I configure environment-specific behavior in the config file?
expected_answer: `defineConfig` accepts a function that receives `{ command, mode }`. Branch on `command === 'build'` or use `loadEnv` to read `.env` files just like in a Vite config.

question: How do I customize the sidebar per URL prefix?
expected_answer: Pass an object to `themeConfig.sidebar` keyed by the URL prefix. Each prefix gets its own array of groups, allowing different sidebars for `/guide/` vs `/reference/` etc.

question: How do I disable the prev/next links at the bottom of pages?
expected_answer: Set `themeConfig.docFooter = { prev: false, next: false }` globally, or use frontmatter `prev: false` / `next: false` on a single page. You can also pass strings to override the displayed text.

question: How do I add a global footer below page content?
expected_answer: Set `themeConfig.footer = { message, copyright }`. The footer is hidden on pages where the right-side aside is shown unless explicitly forced.

question: How do I add a Carbon Ads banner?
expected_answer: Set `themeConfig.carbonAds = { code, placement }`. The default theme renders the ad in the right-side aside when both fields are provided.

question: How do I read site data and theme config inside a component?
expected_answer: Call `useData()` and read `site.value` for site-level config and `theme.value` for `themeConfig`. Both are reactive refs.

question: How do I write a CMS-backed VitePress site?
expected_answer: Use a build-time data loader (`createContentLoader` or `defineLoader`) that fetches from your CMS and returns the page list. For runtime CMS data, fetch inside `<script setup>` guarded by `<ClientOnly>` for SSR safety.
